lineage_context.teaching_goal: Use the large rhizomatous monocot habit, highly asymmetric flower, one fertile petaloid stamen, inferior multiovulate ovary, and warty many-seeded capsule to separate Cannaceae from Marantaceae.

project_scope.note: Cannaceae contains a single genus, Canna. Canna glauca is accepted and native in Texas under current Kew; strict project county-range approval remains a separate species workflow.

family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: Start with the flower, not the leaf. Cannaceae has a strongly asymmetric flower with only one fertile stamen; that stamen is petaloid and bears a single fertile anther theca along one edge. Then confirm an inferior 3-locular ovary with many ovules.
family_diagnostics.vegetative: Large rhizomatous perennial herbs with broad entire leaves and open sheathing bases; leaves are arranged distichously to spirally and lack a ligule.
family_diagnostics.reproductive: Flowers bisexual, strongly asymmetric and showy. There are 3 sepals and 3 petals, but much of the showy display is made by petaloid staminodes. Only one stamen is fertile, and its anther is monothecal/one-thecous along the margin of the petaloid stamen.
family_diagnostics.fruit: A loculicidal capsule, commonly warty or tuberculate, containing many hard globose seeds.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: Big canna-like leaf + asymmetric flower + one fertile petaloid stamen + warty many-seeded capsule = Cannaceae.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: rhizomatous broad-leaved monocot → asymmetric flower → one fertile petaloid stamen → flat petaloid style → warty capsule/hard seeds → Marantaceae comparison
visual_lesson.intro: Cannaceae and Marantaceae are close relatives and both make strange asymmetric flowers. The fastest split is what the fertile stamen, style and ovary are doing.

steps.title: 1 · Separate petals from petaloid staminodes
steps.look_for: Three actual petals plus several large petal-like sterile staminal structures.
steps.why_it_matters: Much of what looks like the corolla in Canna is actually modified staminal tissue.

steps.title: 2 · Find the one fertile stamen
steps.look_for: One petal-like fertile stamen with a single narrow anther theca running along one margin.
steps.why_it_matters: This is one of the defining Zingiberales characters and a major Cannaceae confirmation trait.

steps.title: 3 · Find the flat petaloid style
steps.look_for: A broad flattened petaloid style with the stigmatic area at the tip/margin.
steps.why_it_matters: Marantaceae instead uses a more specialized hook-shaped style involved in its trigger pollination mechanism.

steps.title: 4 · Inspect the ovary and fruit surface
steps.look_for: Inferior 3-locular ovary with many ovules; mature capsule is warty/tuberculate and many-seeded.
steps.why_it_matters: This sharply contrasts with Marantaceae's one-ovule-per-locule pattern.

steps.title: 5 · Learn the seed
steps.look_for: Smooth, very hard, rounded seeds inside the capsule.
steps.why_it_matters: This reinforces the many-ovule/many-seed Cannaceae plan.

comparisons.title: Cannaceae vs Marantaceae
comparisons.rule: Cannaceae: one fertile monothecal petaloid stamen, flat petaloid style, axile placentae with many ovules per locule, warty many-seeded capsule. Marantaceae: one fertile monothecal stamen plus highly specialized hooded/callose staminodes, hook-shaped style, usually one ovule per locule, and only 1–3 seeds.

comparisons.title: Cannaceae vs Zingiberaceae
comparisons.rule: Both have strongly modified asymmetric flowers, but Canna has broad petaloid staminodes and a single marginal one-theca anther on a petaloid stamen; gingers usually have a conspicuous labellum formed from fused staminodes and aromatic rhizomes.

visual_lesson.caveat: Do not identify Cannaceae from broad leaves alone; bananas, gingers and Marantaceae can look similar vegetatively. The flower and fruit are much safer.

genera.fast_cue: broad rhizomatous herb + asymmetric flower + one fertile petaloid stamen + warty many-seeded capsule

visual_targets.structure: one fertile petaloid stamen with marginal monothecal anther
visual_targets.annotation_goal: label fertile anther edge versus sterile petaloid tissue
contrast directly with Marantaceae hook-shaped style
connect fruit anatomy to many-seeded family plan
